texts: Two Keepers have left the village.
The two Keepers married outside Aelmere.
When a Keeper leaves a station, the Council assigns an apprentice to the station.
The Council assigns an apprentice who has completed thirty solo nights.

fields.sentence: Two Keepers have left the village.

review.notes: Matches the 'Both dogs barked' pattern exactly — group witness + Cardinality 2 + group event + per-member rule at (STV 1.0 0.9) sharing the definite sk_village_1 — and the present perfect correctly coarsens to Past with no Before (no second event to order against). The counted 'Two Keepers' rightly takes the capitalized-common-noun default rather than the plural Name-only label route, which applies to a plural label referring as a name.

fields.sentence: The two Keepers married outside Aelmere.

q2_gaps: A COUNTED/individuated capitalized plural kind-word label ("the TWO Keepers"): the instruction set gives the common-noun default for singular-collective labels and a `Name`-only individual (one symbol, `Name` atom, no `GroupOf`, no per-member kind from the label word) for a capitalized plural label "referring as a name", but says nothing about a capitalized plural that a numeral individuates — where the Name-only-individual treatment is incompatible with a `Cardinality` and with two people marrying, so the group + count reading has to be inferred.
review.notes: Everything downstream of that label choice is right: reciprocal "married" stays collective on the group symbol with no per-member rule, `Cardinality 2` rides the group, and the non-containment spatial PP keeps its surface preposition head `Outside` (a `Location aelmere` atom would have wrongly asserted in-ness).

fields.sentence: When a Keeper leaves a station, the Council assigns an apprentice to the station.
parse: (: keeper_leave_assign (Implication (And (Member $k keeper) (Member $s station) (Member $e leave) (Agent $e $k) (Source $e $s)) (And (Member (sk_assign $k $s) assign) (Agent (sk_assign $k $s) sk_council_1) (Theme (sk_assign $k $s) (sk_apprentice $k $s)) (Member (sk_apprentice $k $s) apprentice) (Recipient (sk_assign $k $s) $s))) (STV 1.0 0.9))

q1_issues.issue: The rule emits no (During <response-event> <trigger-event>) atom, which the 'every time / whenever' occurrence machinery that bare 'when P, Q' with indefinite participants routes to mandates.

The consequent Skolem terms are keyed to the participants (sk_assign $k $s) rather than to the trigger occurrence, so two separate leavings by the same Keeper from the same station collapse into a single assign event instead of one per occurrence.
(Source $e $s) puts the bare direct object of 'leaves a station' into a preposition-named oblique the text never uses, where the direct-object test ('does the object itself change?') gives Theme.
(Recipient (sk_assign $k $s) $s) makes a place the goal of a transfer, where Recipient is defined for a transfer goal / addressee of communication and a non-recipient 'to' takes Goal.

review.notes: Routing is right (indefinite trigger participants -> rule, not two plain events), as are the anaphoric 'the station' bound to the premise variable $s, the dependent-existential Skolem apprentice with its class atom inside the consequent, sk_council_1 as a top-level-asserted constant used only in the conclusion, and the 1.0/0.9 rule TV with no QuantifierPhrase companion.

issues.reason: Bare "when P, Q" with indefinite participants routes to "exactly the whenever machinery", whose stated form ties the per-occurrence response to its trigger with During — (During (sk_bark $x) $x) in the bell/dog example — so the atom is mandated and simply absent.

That machinery mints "the response as a Skolem event per occurrence", keyed to the trigger event variable, so keying to ($k $s) gives one assign per keeper-station pair and silently identifies two separate leavings by the same Keeper at the same station.

"leaves a station" takes a bare direct object, and the set reserves preposition-named/oblique slots for objects the verb takes with a preposition while a direct object goes by the change test — the station is not created, destroyed or changed, so Theme.

Recipient is the goal of a transfer or the addressee of communication — a party — with a non-recipient "to" explicitly taking the spatial Goal ("muttered to the bailiff … never the spatial Goal" draws the line the other way), so a station, a place/post, is a Goal.

adjudication.defect_summary: Compliant form keys the consequent Skolems to the trigger occurrence — (sk_assign $e) and (sk_apprentice $e) — and adds (During (sk_assign $e) $e); the premise's (Source $e $s) becomes (Theme $e $s); the consequent's (Recipient … $s) becomes (Goal (sk_assign $e) $s).
adjudication.notes: Routing to a rule rather than two plain events, binding the anaphoric "the station" to the premise variable, asserting sk_council_1 at top level while using it only in the conclusion, and the (STV 1.0 0.9) rule TV with no QuantifierPhrase companion are all correct.

fields.sentence: The Council assigns an apprentice who has completed thirty solo nights.

q2_gaps: a habitual/policy clause whose object is an indefinite restricted by a relative clause ("assigns an apprentice who has completed thirty solo nights") — Existential forces "an N" under a verbal predicate to a witness, and a singular collective subject to a plain no-rule event, so the eligibility-criterion reading has no route and the parse ends up asserting one specific apprentice who has completed thirty nights
review.notes: "The Council" correctly stays a capitalized-common-noun witness with no Name atom; present perfect maps to coarse Past with no Before (that ordering is past-perfect-only); the counted plural object takes GroupOf plus Cardinality 30. Exposing (Inheritance solo_night solo) treats solo as a predicable adjective, a borderline call against the gradable/positional/material exposure list.
